source.title: Leader Stochastic Gradient Descent for Distributed Training of Deep Learning Models
source.authors: Yunfei Teng; Wen-Bo Gao; F. Chalus; A. Choromańska; D. Goldfarb; Adrian Weller

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the full paper and supplementary material; no truncation or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Compares test error for several distributed training optimizers on natural image classification tasks, using a different intervention from the listed claim versions. It does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, adaptive optimizers, batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness measures, or example removal.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error comparisons for LSGD, EASGD, DataParallel, LARS, and, where shown, SGD. The text supplies qualitative comparisons, while the plotted values are figure-only. Large-batch generalization claims in the introduction are cited background, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study cites large-batch generalization penalties as background, but reports comparisons of distributed optimizers against wall-clock time. It does not report a controlled batch-size comparison under a fixed epoch budget or test any other listed version. Batch sizes explored during tuning are selection values, not batch-size results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that leader-based distributed optimization is theoretically justified and empirically well-suited to matrix completion and deep-network training, with favorable comparisons against selected distributed baselines.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an asynchronous leader-based distributed optimizer with momentum and weight decay; compares it with EASGD, DataParallel, LARS, and SGD rather than the original claim's interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ across network and dataset settings and, for ResNet20, between 4 and 12 workers. The paper reports selected hyperparameters yielding the smallest achievable test error under similar convergence rates.

fits_no_version.finding: LSGD improves convergence speed against selected distributed baselines on CIFAR-10, obtains better test error in several reported comparisons, and performs comparably to LARS on ImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Leader-based distributed training can improve convergence speed and held-out performance relative to selected parallel-training methods under the study's tuned recipes.

record.problems: Test-error values are shown in figures without numerical extraction in the supplied text. The paper reports optimal hyperparameter choices for similar convergence rates, so comparisons are tuned comparisons. It does not evaluate random-label memorization or measure training-test gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for each comparator were extracted because the supplied text gives qualitative comparisons and the plotted per-method values are figure-only; rows capture the stated outcome by model and setting.

untested.parts: Joint random-label memorization and natural-label generalization, including chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under limited tuning, and the specified recovery conditions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and whether recipe changes remove a batch-size penalty.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, generalization gaps, and ranking against other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The proposed T2 classification is inconsistent with all eight versions being untested. LARS comparisons alone do not establish V4, and changing worker counts or tuning batch sizes alone does not establish V5. Claims about wide valleys are motivation rather than measurements of V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum SGD under the specified tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: CNN7 on CIFAR-10, LSGD
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error for the center variable versus wall-clock time across training methods.

conditions.value: 4 or 12; text states LSGD is roughly 1.5 times faster than EASGD for 12 workers

rows.note: Authors state LSGD consistently outperforms competitors in convergence speed; the plotted test-error values are not transcribed.
rows.check: This is a comparison of the study's optimizer with other methods, not a measurement of a listed claim. Section 4.2 reports faster convergence; numerical test-error values are unavailable in the supplied text. Split the combined 4- and 12-worker conditions if retaining these results.

rows.subject: VGG16 on CIFAR-10, LSGD
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error for the center variable versus wall-clock time across training methods.
rows.note: Authors state LSGD obtains a much better solution than other methods and marginally faster convergence than EASGD.
rows.check: The qualitative improvement is supported by Section 4.2, but it compares distributed optimization methods and bears on no listed version. The row combines worker settings and lacks numerical test errors.

rows.subject: ResNet20 on CIFAR-10, LSGD
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error for the center variable versus wall-clock time across training methods.
rows.note: Authors state LSGD converges comparably fast to EASGD but recovers better test error.
rows.check: Better test error than EASGD with 4 workers is explicitly reported, but this method comparison does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet20 on CIFAR-10, LSGD
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error for the center variable versus wall-clock time across training methods.
rows.note: Authors state LSGD converges roughly 1.5 times faster than EASGD and obtains significantly smaller error.
rows.check: Faster convergence and smaller error than EASGD with 12 workers are explicitly reported, but this method comparison does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet50 on ImageNet, LSGD
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error for the center variable versus wall-clock time across training methods.
rows.note: Authors say LSGD behaves comparably to LARS and converges much faster than EASGD; SGD was omitted from the plot.
rows.check: Comparable performance to LARS does not establish a partial effect for any listed version. This is a distributed-method comparison without a controlled batch-size or limited-tuning adaptive-optimizer experiment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
